sentences.text: Lay a straightedge from the light horizontally to the side scale, and read forty-one degrees, ten point two minutes north.
Next, measure with the dividers from the nearest meridian, seventy-one degrees thirty minutes west, to the light.
Carry that to the top scale, and it spans four point six minutes.
Because the light is west of the meridian, and west longitude increases to the west, add: seventy-one degrees thirty-four point six minutes west.
The answer is forty-one degrees ten point two north, seventy-one degrees thirty-four point six west.
